description: The figure is a two-level pie/sunburst chart illustrating a taxonomy of medical ethics, with an inner ring showing four pillar principles and an outer ring subdividing these into 26 labeled categories. The inner ring contains 4 slices labeled Beneficence (blue, visually the largest at roughly about two-fifths of the circle), Autonomy (green, about one-quarter), Non-Maleficence (lavender/purple, about one-fifth), and Justice (orange, about one-sixth). The outer ring contains 26 slices grouped by the inner principle and matching its color: under Beneficence (blue) there are 11 categories—“Recognize the Responsibility of the Occupation,” “Comply with Laws and Regulations,” “Provide Medical Care to Patients,” “Continual Learning,” “Provide Assistance in Emergency,” “Respect and Cooperate with Colleagues,” “Respect Life, Dignity of Patients,” “Give Priority to Patient’s Interest in Conflict of Interest,” “Minimizing Conflicts of Interest,” “Ethical research,” and “Open Discussion and Fair Charging of Fees”—with each wedge taking a small fraction of the full circle (collectively spanning the Beneficence sector). Under Autonomy (green) there are 7 categories—“Respect Patient’s Rights to be Informed, Freedom of Choice,” “Respect Decision making of Incompetent/Competent Patient,” “Maintain Truthful, Factual Communication,” “Keep Confidential of Patient’s Information,” “Professional Relationship with Patients and Their Relatives,” “Make Responsible and Independent Clinical Judgement,” and “Physician Can Freely Choose Whom to Serve.” Under Non-Maleficence (purple) there are 4 categories—“Prevent Patient from Harm,” “Maintain Qualified When Providing Medical Care,” “Report Unethical and Unprofessional Conduct,” and “Do Not Use Medicine for Personal Gain.” Under Justice (orange) there are 4 categories—“Treat Patients Fairly and Equally,” “Allocate Medical Sources Fairly,” “Promote Environmental Sustainability,” and “Promote the Health of Community and Public Education.” The chart does not show a legend or numeric percentage labels; instead, text labels are placed directly inside the slices, and the segments are arranged around the circle by principle grouping rather than being presented as an explicitly size-sorted sequence, with no slices visually exploded or offset.
